text:
Lina: FYI - we promoted nightingale-q5-int4 to the canary ring and seeing an uptick in structured-output parse failures specifically when toolcall objects cross batch-slice boundaries. numbers: baseline 0.5% -> canary 3.6% (n=2100).
Omar: can you paste a minimal repro from the stream assembler?
Lina: snippet from the stream logs:
```
INVOKE id=zz-201 model=nightingale-q5 slice=22/56
OUT >> {\"tool\":\"search\",\"args\":{\"q\":\"vintage sourdough tips\",\"k\":6}
...<slice ends mid-json>...
---next slice---
INVOKE cont id=zz-201 slice=23/56
OUT >> ,\"meta\":{\"cursor\":\"abc\"}}
parser: JSONError: unexpected token ',' at position 1
```
Priya: interesting. this is not only EOFs; we're getting unexpected-token when the array/object boundary gets split and the assembler hands incomplete fragments to the JSON parser.
Kai: likely root cause: quant-int4 nudged tokenization so deterministic slice cutpoints now fall inside punctuation/structural tokens more often. even a one-token shift can change where a comma or brace sits.
bench-bot: Canary digest: nightingale-q5-int4 parse failures = 3.6%; breakdown: 50% unexpected token, 35% unexpected EOF, 15% base64 decode errors (long strings); link: https://redwood.internal/canary/1797777777
Omar: mitigation ideas (quick list):
- assembler: buffer-until-balanced-braces (cheap heuristic)
- overlap-replay: prepend last N tokens of previous slice during reassembly
- sentinel-suffix: append explicit EOF sentinel in tool prompts (e.g., "__TOOL_DONE__")
- tokenizer-diff: run tokenization delta vs fp16 to pick overlap size
Priya: ordering: buffer-until-balanced is the least invasive so try that first as a runtime flag. if it reduces >70% we keep.
Lina: I worry about latency impact if we block too long waiting for balance in slow streams. can we do a bounded wait (e.g., 150ms) then try overlap fallback?
Kai: yes, bounded buffer + overlap fallback seems pragmatic: buffer for up to X ms, if still unbalanced then request extra slice or try overlap merge. also we should add a preflight lint on the first chunk that cheaply detects likely mid-json (unbalanced braces, odd trailing comma or open string) and tag those invocations for special handling.
Omar: telemetry changes: add tags `reassembly:buffered`, `reassembly:overlap_used`, `preflight:midjson_detected`, `sentinel:used`. need counts to know which path is doing the heavy lifting.
Priya: another class we saw: long base64 fields (thumbnails) get chopped and produce decode errors even though JSON parser succeeds. solution: length-pref for binary blobs or base64 url-safe with explicit padding sentinel. length-pref is my fav - assembler validates len before decode.
Kai: agree. length-pref is backward compatible if assembler tolerates missing len. implement as opt-in flag for canary.
Lina: plan proposal:
1) land runtime flags: `buffer_until_balanced` (bounded 150ms), `overlap_tokens=16`, `sentinel_suffix` (off), `length_pref_b64` (off).
2) run micro-canary: enable buffer_until_balanced + overlap_tokens=12 for 30m with same traffic, reduce batch-slice size from 56->40 to isolate effects.
3) collect raw failure payloads for offline repair analysis and run a tokenizer-diff corpus between fp16/int4 to see distribution of token-shifts.
4) if buffer+overlap reduces errors >80% then enable sentinel-suffix A/B for next round to see if model-side sentinel is cleaner.
Omar: I'll prototype a cheap assembler change today: buffer until braces balance OR 150ms whichever comes first; implement overlap-merger as fallback. keep CPU cost minimal.
Priya: I'll add length-pref handling in the image.attach schema and a parser len-check in assembler. will enable heuristic buffering for existing base64-like fields as stopgap.
bench-bot: queued a collector job to fetch the 200 most recent boundary failures -> s3://canary-dumps/nq5-boundary-samples/; uploaded samples will include both assembled and raw slice fragments.
Lina: timelines? can we have flags ready to toggle by tomorrow AM?
Kai: yes, Omar will push the assembler toggles today. Priya will push the len-pref support and heuristic buffer. I will coordinate micro-canary config and telemetry tagging.
Omar: one more: I'm adding a reassembly checksum field for debug only - assembler will compute a lightweight rolling hash on merged tokens so we can quickly diff failing vs succeeding reassemblies. helpful for triage.
Priya: also recommend we add a tiny post-parse repair attempt on failure: try simple repairs (append ']}' , close open strings) for diagnostics, but count repaired vs native success separately so we don't hide regressions.
Lina: good call. let's keep this thread for micro-canary numbers and paste raw failed fragments here as we collect them. I'll enable pinned message to collate key links.
infra-bot: ticket RF-9754 created: "nightingale-q5: stream-reassembly & base64 chunking triage". attaching telemetry dashboard and upload bucket.
Lina: thanks all 389. will post first micro-canary snapshot once it's done.
